community.tagline: Single-row homes for the life of your dreams
community.subtitle: A life of joy and harmony at The Valley
intro: NARA is The Valley’s second townhouse community by Emaar: 372 single-row townhouses with 3 and 4 bedrooms, in a choice of three contemporary designs – Aston, Palma and Charm.
The homes are set around a series of integrated parks. Pleasant pathways, stunning landscaping and green spaces give families ample room to enjoy the moments that matter, outdoors.

THE VALLEY is a gated community on Dubai – Al Ain Road, a major link between Dubai and Abu Dhabi: a friendly town centre, playgrounds and parks for children to run free, a golden beach for lazy days and plenty of opportunities to focus on health and wellbeing – all within easy reach.

sheet.convention: continuous sheet pixel coordinates, pixel (i,j) covering [i,i+1)x[j,j+1): px = ox + x*pxPerM, py = oy + z*pxPerM (independent NCC registration of the JSON walls, about +-0.3 px)

A3A.notes: Reference trace for the 3BR mid-unit family (A3A/A3C/C3A identical interiors; A3B/C3B their mirror). Right party wall returns 2.3 m along the terrace (supports the balcony side), pump room enclosure at the front-left. Traced from the 1200x800 developer sheet (only source; ~3.7 cm per pixel). Scale = least-squares fit of the printed clear room dimensions on the A3A sheet (23 dims, 27.0 px/m, rms 0.04 m; first printed number = drawing x / across the plot, second = z / depth); the five 3BR sheets are exported at slightly different zooms, so each sheet was registered to A3A on its wall faces (scale + shift, mirrored for B) and pxPerM is A3A's value times that sheet's factor. Wall faces are sub-pixel measurements of the solid black strokes (about +-0.03 m). First floor aligned to the ground floor on the party walls, stair walls and street plot line. Plot = outline as drawn = OUTER faces of both party walls (each sheet draws the full party-wall thickness), so neighbouring plots overlap by one party wall (~0.25 m): place adjacent units at a pitch of plot.w - 0.25 m. Walls are continuous through openings; each opening lies on the centre-line of walls[opening.wall] (cut it out; lintel above 'head', sill below 'sill'). Door 'hinge'/'swingTo' = hinge point and the tip of the open leaf. Walls with 'h' are low/boundary elements (garden walls 1.2, fence 1.2, pump/utility enclosure 2.2 (Aston pump room) / 2.95 (Charm utility, up to the canopy), carport columns 3.2, balustrades 1.0-1.1, under-stair walls 1.4 / 2.3 - they stop under the stair soffit); kind 'doorFrame' walls are thin door lines with no solid wall above head height worth modelling. rot = degrees clockwise on the drawing (x right, z down; 0 = back to -z, facing +z), i.e. three.js rotation.y = -rot*pi/180; facing = (-sin rot, cos rot). Fixture w = side-to-side, d = front-to-back. Stair: U-shaped with two 2-winder corners, 21 risers x 0.171 m = 3.6 m (riser count read from the drawn nosings on both floors); flight 3 and the upper winders run ABOVE the kitchen counter (dashed on the ground-floor sheet), so the kitchen counter sits under the stair soffit; use treadPolys[].top for exact tread heights. FF 'voids' = stairwell (no slab). Levels (3.6 / 6.9 / 7.9) are typical Emaar G+1 values, not from drawings; sill/head heights are assumptions. Open-plan splits (living/dining/kitchen/hall) are virtual lines placed so the printed dims fit. Doors without a drawn swing (maid's room - leaf not drawn at all -, maid's bath, powder, storage, master bath) are given an assumed swing. The small white recess drawn inside the hall-side party wall (~0.5 m long) is ignored (likely a DB niche). Facade fins/angled canopy blades of the Aston street elevation are only partly represented (party-wall fins). Furniture is read from the drawn symbols, positions within ~0.1 m; sizes are standard. 'Total area' in the sheet table is Emaar's figure per unit (the drawn plot of A3A, 7.93 x 23.70 m = 187.9 m2, happens to equal the 5-plex A TH04 figure; other units' figures differ although the drawing is the same). [VERIFIER 2026-10-20: this file was normalised to the common schema shared by all 16 plans - plot party side on the party-wall centre-line (x shifted where needed), garden walls/gates in floors.ground.boundary, balustrades in floors.*.railings, carport canopy in canopies[], door hinge = point + swingTo, voids as {type, poly}; statements above about plot edges, boundary/fence/balustrade walls, wall heights of site elements, canopy heights and hinge a/b describe the tracer's original file. See verification.changes; QA images in pipeline/verify/plans/<KEY>.png.]
